beats.say: Colgan Air's flight to Buffalo got a stall warning. The captain pulled the wrong way, and {fact24} people died.

beats.say: February {fact2}, {fact1}. The twin-propeller airliner was slowing for the runway, its airspeed sagging to {fact7} knots.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the airliner glides out of the cloud, its landing lights on
the two propellers blur in the lights
the landing gear swings down
the airspeed tag counts down and turns red

beats.say: The control column shook: the wings were close to a stall. The trained answer is to push forward. The captain pulled back.

moments.what: both control columns judder, the STALL light flashes
a red band lights on the airspeed tape
a green arrow points the column forward
the captain's column comes back, a red arrow

beats.say: The nose rose, a wing dropped, and in under half a minute the airliner came down on a house, {fact5} nautical miles from the airport.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the airliner's nose rises
the left wing drops, the plane rolls
a clock tag runs
the plane is gone into cloud; far below, an orange glow among houses

beats.say: This crash had no single cause. It was a chain: an airspeed set too low for the ice, talk where there should be silence, a warning nobody called, and one wrong reflex.

link one writes on

beats.say: Here it is in seven parts: the flight, the wing, the ice, the cue, the last half minute, the findings, and the law that came after.

beats.say: The plane was a Bombardier Q four hundred, a turboprop airliner, flown by Colgan Air as a Continental Connection flight.

params.place: the ramp at Newark airport at night

moments.what: the chapter card types on; the camera finds the airliner at the gate
a label pins on its propeller
a tag names the airline
a second tag names the brand it flew for

beats.say: Where was it going? That evening, from Newark, near New York City, to Buffalo, in the far west of New York State.

params.place: a map of the north-east United States

moments.what: the map of the north-east draws in
a pin drops on Newark
the city lights glow
the route line draws to Buffalo
Buffalo's pin pulses

beats.say: High winds had slowed flights at Newark all day. This one took off more than two hours behind schedule, into the dark, bound for Buffalo.

params.place: the runway at Newark at night

moments.what: snow streaks sideways past the gate lights
a line of waiting planes' lights
the airliner rolls and lifts off
it climbs into the cloud

beats.say: Who was aboard? {fact3} people: the two pilots, two flight attendants, and the passengers, some of them going home.

params.place: a cut-away of the airliner's cabin

moments.what: the cabin cut-away draws in
two figures light in the flight deck
two figures light by the doors
the seat rows fill with small figures
the reading lights glow warm

beats.say: And the crew? The first officer lived near Seattle. To reach work, she had flown overnight, across the country through Memphis, into Newark that morning.

params.place: a map of the United States at night

moments.what: a pin lights near Seattle
a moon rises over the map
the line bends through Memphis
it ends at Newark at dawn

beats.say: Climbing out, the crew switched on the de-icing systems, which crack ice off the wings. The plane levelled at {fact11} feet.

params.place: above the cloud deck over Pennsylvania at night

moments.what: the airliner climbs through cloud
the black boots on the wings' front edges pulse
it levels off, an altitude tag types on

beats.say: Up there, the autopilot flew and the pilots talked almost the whole way. Was that allowed? At that height, yes.

params.place: the airliner's flight deck at night, seen from behind the pilots

moments.what: the AP light glows green
speech marks bob between the two pilots
the altimeter reads the cruise height
a small tick stamps by it

beats.say: Was the weather the problem? There was light snow and mist near Buffalo, with ice in the cloud: nothing unusual for a winter night there.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the airliner descends through thin cloud
snow streaks thicken past the wing
a grey haze drifts below
the town's lights glow faintly far below

beats.say: But near Buffalo, the cloud was full of ice. And ice changes the one thing that keeps a wing in the air.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the airliner sinks into grey cloud
white rime creeps along the wing's front edge
the white crust thickens along the wing's front edge
the camera slides along the iced wing

beats.say: What keeps a wing up? Air flows over its curved top and under it, and the wing turns that flow into lift.

params.place: a wind tunnel of night air around the airliner's wing section

moments.what: the chapter card types on; the wing section draws
streamlines run past it
the top curve traces in blue
a big lift arrow rises

beats.say: Tilt the wing up a little, and it makes more lift. That tilt against the oncoming air is called the angle of attack.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the airliner's nose tilts up against the oncoming snow
the snow streaks bend under the wing
an angle arc draws between the wing and the airflow
the ANGLE OF ATTACK label types on

beats.say: Past a certain angle, the air can't follow the top any more. It breaks away in swirls, and the lift collapses. That is a stall.

params.place: a wind tunnel of night air around the airliner's wing section

moments.what: the wing tilts further
the streamlines peel off the top
swirls tumble behind the wing
the lift arrow shrinks and turns red
a STALL stamp lands

beats.say: A slow plane needs a bigger angle to hold itself up. So as the airspeed bleeds away, the wing creeps toward that edge.

params.place: a wind tunnel of night air around the airliner's wing section

moments.what: the speed dial falls
the wing tilts up to keep its lift
the dial needle slides down
a red line marks the stall angle; the wing's angle closes on it

beats.say: What warns the crew? This plane has a stick shaker. Near the edge, it rattles both control columns and sounds a warning.

params.place: the airliner's flight deck at night, seen from behind the pilots

moments.what: the flight deck lights dim
the motor on each column is ringed
both columns judder
the STALL light flashes red

beats.say: If that isn't enough, a stick pusher shoves the column forward, to lower the nose and get the air flowing again.

params.place: the airliner's flight deck at night, seen from behind the pilots

moments.what: the columns keep shaking
the pusher is ringed under the floor
both columns slide forward with a green arrow
the nose on the horizon drops

beats.say: Pilots are trained for this moment. Nose down to cut the angle, power up to get speed back, and the wing grips the air again.

params.place: a wind tunnel of night air around the airliner's wing section

moments.what: a training card pins on
the wing tilts down
a thrust arrow grows
the streamlines reattach and glow green

beats.say: Ice on the front of a wing can make it stall sooner, at a higher speed. That night, the airliner had ice. Did it matter?

params.place: a wind tunnel of night air around the airliner's wing section

moments.what: a rough white crust grows on the leading edge
the red stall line moves down to a smaller angle
the background darkens to night
a question mark stamps

beats.say: The pilots saw it. Ice was building on the windshield and on the front edges of the wings.

params.place: beside the airliner's flight deck windows in the cloud

moments.what: the chapter card types on; the camera looks along the cockpit windows
rime spreads across the windshield
the first officer's words type on as text
the camera slides out along the iced wing

beats.say: What do pilots do about ice? The plane has a switch called ref speeds. Set to increase, it makes the stall warning come sooner, to leave more margin.

params.place: the overhead panel above the captain's seat

moments.what: the overhead panel lights
the camera finds the ref speeds switch
the switch flips to INCREASE
the shaker's trigger slides earlier on a scale
a margin bracket opens

beats.say: On the airspeed tape, a red and black band shows where the shaker will fire. With the switch on, the band sat about {fact15} knots higher.

params.place: the captain's airspeed display on the flight deck

moments.what: the airspeed tape scrolls
the red and black band glows at the bottom
a small INCREASE label lights
the band slides up the tape by the figure

beats.say: The switch was on. So what speed did they plan? For landing, the crew briefed a speed of {fact6} knots, the speed for a wing with no ice.

params.place: the captain's airspeed display on the flight deck

moments.what: the INCREASE label glows
a question mark blinks by the speed bug
the speed bug slides into place
a briefing card pins on
a small wing icon draws on the card
a NO ICE tag stamps on the card

beats.say: So the warning would fire {fact29} knots above the speed they meant to land at. To slow down to it, they'd have to fly through the warning.

params.place: the captain's airspeed display on the flight deck

moments.what: the band's top edge lights red
a bracket measures from the bug up to the band
the tape starts to scroll down
the bug disappears under the red band

beats.say: And the ice itself? The investigators found it barely hurt the wing. The aircraft could still fly normally. The danger was in the numbers.

params.place: a wind tunnel of night air around the airliner's wing section

moments.what: the iced wing section returns
the ice crust fades to a thin line
the streamlines run smooth and green
the speed bug and the red band slide in beside the wing

beats.say: Someone had to watch that speed closely. But below ten thousand feet, the flight deck was not quiet.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the airliner sinks through the cloud
its landing lights flare
a caption types on: below ten thousand feet
speech marks blink over the lit cockpit windows

beats.say: What is the sterile cockpit? Below {fact12} feet, the rule allows only talk that is about flying the plane.

params.place: the airliner's flight deck at night, seen from behind the pilots

moments.what: the chapter card types on; the altimeter winds past the mark
a STERILE COCKPIT sign lights over the windshield
the speech marks shrink
a checklist card pins on

beats.say: On this flight, the pilots kept up a conversation that had nothing to do with flying, down through the descent.

params.place: beside the airliner's lit cockpit windows in the snow

moments.what: the camera glides past the lit cockpit windows, two pilots inside
speech marks bob over the windows
a STERILE COCKPIT sign blinks red
the airliner keeps sinking through the snow

beats.say: At {fact13} feet, the autopilot held the height, and the captain pulled the power back to slow down for landing.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the airliner levels off under the cloud, an altitude tag types on
an AP tag lights
the propellers slow
the plane eases back in the frame

beats.say: Who controls the speed? This airliner had no autothrottle. Power was set by hand, and only the pilots could notice the speed falling short.

params.place: the airliner's flight deck at night, seen from behind the pilots

moments.what: the camera finds the power levers
an AUTOTHROTTLE label is crossed out
the captain's hand rests on the levers
a speed arrow on the screen points down

beats.say: The first officer was busy: the landing gear, a radio change, a chime to the cabin, then a check that the gear was down.

params.place: the airliner's flight deck at night, seen from behind the pilots

moments.what: the first officer turns to the centre panel
the gear lever drops, three lights
the radio frequency flips
a chime icon rings
three green gear lights tick

beats.say: Was there a warning? Meanwhile, the red band climbed the airspeed tape toward the falling speed. It was there to see for {fact14} seconds.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the tape scrolls down
the red band rises from the bottom
the speed box ticks down
a timer counts the figure

beats.say: The autopilot raised the nose to hold the height. The speed numbers turned red. Neither pilot said anything about it.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the airliner's nose creeps up
an altitude-hold tag lights
the airspeed tag turns red
the cockpit windows stay quiet

beats.say: The investigators wrote that the cues were on the instruments with enough time to act, but neither pilot responded.

params.place: an investigator's desk

moments.what: the report page settles on the desk
the camera pushes in on the paragraph
the line highlights
the line underlines

beats.say: Three small lapses so far: the speed, the talk, the cue. The fourth took less than half a second.

params.place: the investigation board

moments.what: the chain board returns
link one stamps
link two stamps
link three stamps
the fourth box blinks red, empty

beats.say: Then the stick shaker fired, at {fact7} knots. The autopilot switched itself off, with a horn that kept sounding.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the chapter card types on; the clock shows the minute
the whole display judders, STALL in red
the speed box locks on the figure
the AP light goes out
a horn icon pulses

beats.say: Less than half a second later, the captain pulled the column back. A second after that, he pushed the power up, but not to full.

params.place: close on the airliner's nose and cockpit windows in the snow

moments.what: the wings flash red as the shaker fires
the nose heaves up, a big red COLUMN BACK card slams on
the propellers spin harder, a POWER UP card
a NOT FULL stamp lands on it

beats.say: Pulling back raised the angle of attack, the opposite of the trained answer. The wing was already near the edge. Now it went over.

params.place: a wind tunnel of night air around the airliner's wing section

moments.what: the wing tilts up sharply
the green trained arrow flips to red
the angle reaches the red line
the airflow tears off the top in swirls

beats.say: The airliner pitched up, and rolled left to {fact8} degrees, then swung hard back to the right.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the nose rises
the left wing drops
a bank tag shows the figure
the plane swings back right

beats.say: The stick pusher fired and shoved the nose down. The captain pulled against it. It fired twice more.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the nose shoves down, a green PUSH tally mark
the airliner dips
the nose heaves back up, red
two more pushes, two more tally marks

beats.say: The first officer raised the flaps without being asked. That took away lift the wing badly needed. The speed fell to about {fact18} knots.

params.place: along the airliner's wing, close on the flaps

moments.what: the flaps on the wing's back edge start to slide in
they disappear into the wing
the wing glows red
the airspeed tag counts down

beats.say: She then asked about raising the landing gear too. Neither move was in the company's stall recovery procedure, the board found.

params.place: the airliner's flight deck at night, seen from behind the pilots

moments.what: the first officer turns toward the captain
the gear lever is ringed
a procedure card slides in
two red crosses stamp on it

beats.say: Then it rolled right, to {fact17} degrees, almost on its back. Then the nose dropped toward the ground.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the airliner rolls right
the bank tag shows the figure in red
the wings pass vertical
the nose drops below the horizon

beats.say: Moments later, it came down on a house in Clarence Center, {fact5} nautical miles from the airport.

params.place: the snowy street in Clarence Center at night

moments.what: silence; the plane falls into the cloud and is gone
far away and below, a flash of orange among the snowy houses
a place caption types on
the runway lights far off on the horizon

beats.say: All {fact3} people aboard were killed, and {fact4} person in the house.

params.place: the snowy street in Clarence Center at night

moments.what: fire engines' lights flash red and blue in the street
firefighters with lamps walk through the snow
the memorial count types on
the camera holds on the lit street

beats.say: From the stick shaker to the end of the cockpit recording, the flight lasted less than half a minute.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the flight clock runs from the shaker
the clock stops; the recorder line goes flat
the display fades to black
the time span bracket lights

beats.say: The families of the people aboard wanted to know how a working airliner could fall out of the sky. So did the investigators.

params.place: the snowy street in Clarence Center at night

moments.what: candles flicker by a snowy memorial
the street's lights glow
the camera rises over the town
an investigators' tag types on

beats.say: A year later, the National Transportation Safety Board named the probable cause: the captain's inappropriate response to the stick shaker.

params.place: an investigator's desk

moments.what: the chapter card types on; the report page settles
the camera pushes in on the paragraph
the line highlights
the line underlines

beats.say: First, the plane itself. The investigators found no failure of the structure, the engines or any system, and nothing wrong with its ice protection.

params.place: a dark studio around the airliner, for the investigators' check

moments.what: the airliner turns slowly in the dark, whole
a STRUCTURE tick types on
an ENGINES tick types on
a SYSTEMS tick types on
an ICE PROTECTION tick types on

beats.say: It listed four contributing factors: speed not watched against the rising cue, the sterile cockpit not kept, the flight not managed, and Colgan's speed procedures for ice.

params.place: the investigation board

moments.what: the board lights
factor one stamps
factor two stamps
factor three stamps
factor four stamps

beats.say: Why pull back? The board said his response should have been automatic, but looked like startle and confusion.

params.place: a wind tunnel of night air around the airliner's wing section

moments.what: the wing section tilts up again
the green trained arrow lights
a jolt shakes the drawing
arrows swirl around the wing

beats.say: And the stick pusher? He didn't recognise its push as part of the recovery, the board said, and overriding it made the situation worse.

params.place: the investigation board

moments.what: the board lights a new card
the first finding types on
it stamps
the second finding stamps, red

beats.say: And airline stall training then practised only the warning, and how to fly out of it. Not a stall that had already happened.

params.place: a flight simulator hall

moments.what: a simulator room lights, a cockpit box on legs
a WARNING card ticks green
a recover card ticks green
a FULL STALL card stays blank, red

beats.say: Fatigue? The board found the pilots were likely impaired by it, but couldn't say how much. It is not in the probable cause.

params.place: a map of the United States at night

moments.what: the commute map returns with a moon
a LIKELY tag pins on
a scale with a question mark
a NOT IN THE PROBABLE CAUSE stamp lands

beats.say: The board made {fact9} safety recommendations to the Federal Aviation Administration.

params.place: an investigator's desk

moments.what: the recommendations page settles
the camera pushes in
the count plate types on
the line highlights

beats.say: But the families didn't wait for the regulators. They went to Washington.

params.place: the steps of the US Capitol in Washington

moments.what: a row of small figures with photos held up
a clock ticks on the wall
a stack of papers
the Capitol dome draws on

beats.say: In the summer of {fact21}, Congress passed the Airline Safety and Federal Aviation Administration Extension Act, and the president signed it that August.

params.place: the steps of the US Capitol in Washington

moments.what: the chapter card types on; the Capitol glows at dusk
the dome lights
a pen signs the bill on the desk
the bill's title stamps

beats.say: What does it ask? Under the rule that followed in {fact22}, a first officer must hold an airline transport pilot certificate, which normally takes {fact10} flight hours.

params.place: a pilot's logbook on a desk

moments.what: a pilot's logbook opens
a first officer's cap sits on it
the certificate card slides out
the hours counter rolls up to the figure

beats.say: Airlines also had to train pilots to recover from real stalls, in simulators, by {fact23}. And new rest rules gave pilots longer breaks.

params.place: a flight simulator hall

moments.what: a simulator tilts nose up
a FULL STALL card ticks green
the year plate types on
a bed and a clock appear
the clock's rest arc grows

beats.say: The board also asked for warnings that are harder to miss: an amber band above the red one, and a low-speed alarm you can hear.

params.place: the captain's airspeed display on the flight deck

moments.what: the airspeed display returns
the red band glows
an amber band paints above the red one
a horn icon pulses
sound rings spread from it

beats.say: Would that have stopped this crash? That night, the captain had {fact19} flight hours. The first officer had {fact20}. Both were already past the new minimum.

params.place: a pilot's logbook on a desk

moments.what: two logbooks slide in
the left logbook's counter rolls
the right logbook's counter rolls
both bars glow
a red line at the minimum; both bars are above it

beats.say: So hours alone would not have saved this flight. The training and rest rules went after what failed: one reflex, and one watch on the speed.

params.place: the night sky over western New York, in snow and cloud

moments.what: the airliner flies calm through the snow
a STALL TRAINING tick types on
a REST RULES tick types on
THE REFLEX: PUSH types on
WATCH THE SPEED types on

beats.say: An airspeed set too low for the ice. Talk below ten thousand feet. A warning band nobody called. One pull the wrong way.

params.place: the investigation board

moments.what: link one stamps
link two stamps
link three stamps
link four stamps, red
